turns.prompt_text: I would like to create a markdown file that contains every single query I've asked Gemini. it doesn't really have to be markdown it can be Excel or a json, Yaml, or toml or something else, can I find every query on the desktop version somewhere? Or through Google Takeout?
turns.response_html:
To retrieve every query you've ever asked, the most comprehensive method is through Google Takeout, though it requires a bit of navigation to find the specific "Activity" logs.

1. The Official Method: Google Takeout

Google Takeout is the only way to get a bulk dump of your data. However, the data is often delivered in JSON or HTML formats.

  • Step 1: Head to takeout.google.com.
  • Step 2: Click Deselect all at the top.
  • Step 3: Scroll down to My Activity and check the box.
  • Step 4: This is the crucial part: click the button that says "All activity data included."
  • Step 5: In the pop-up, click Deselect all, then scroll to find and check Gemini Apps (or "Gemini Apps Activity"). Click OK.
  • Step 6: (Optional) If you have custom Gemini Gems you’ve created, scroll to the separate Gemini category on the main list and select that as well.
  • Step 7: Scroll to the bottom, click Next step, and choose your delivery method (usually an email link to a .zip file).

2. Formatting Your Data (Markdown/Excel/JSON)

Since Google Takeout typically exports your activity as a technical JSON file or a set of HTML files, it won't be in Markdown or Excel format immediately.

Given your background in software engineering, the most efficient route is to take that JSON and run a quick script to transform it. Here is a Python template you can use to convert the MyActivity.json from Takeout into a clean Markdown file or a CSV for Excel:

import json
import csv

# Load your Takeout data
with open('MyActivity.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

# Option A: Export to Markdown
with open('gemini_history.md', 'w') as md_file:
    for entry in data:
        title = entry.get('title', 'No Title')
        time = entry.get('time', 'Unknown Time')
        # Queries are usually stored in 'title' or 'titlePayload'
        md_file.write(f"## {time}\n\n**Query:** {title.replace('Searched for ', '')}\n\n---\n\n")

# Option B: Export to CSV (for Excel)
with csv.writer(open('gemini_history.csv', 'w', newline='')) as csv_file:
    writer = csv.writer(csv_file)
    writer.writerow(['Timestamp', 'Query'])
    for entry in data:
        writer.writerow([entry.get('time'), entry.get('title')])

3. Alternative: Browser Extensions

If you prefer a "one-click" solution directly from the desktop version without wrangling JSON files, there are several Chrome/Edge extensions (like Gemini Exporter or SaveChat) that can:

  • Auto-scroll through your history.
  • Scrape the conversations.
  • Download them directly as Markdown (.md), PDF, or JSON.

4. Direct UI Export (Individual Only)

On the desktop version (gemini.google.com), there is no native "Export All" button yet. You can only export individual chats by clicking the Share & export icon (the three dots or share symbol) below a response and selecting "Export to Docs," which you can then download as an industrial-standard file.
